terms.grammar: adverb; utcumque est (erit), however that is (will be)
evidence: Liv. praef. 3: utcumque erit, juvābit tamen
terms.comment: The main clause usually carries tamen, “all the same” (see however).

terms.register: vōx cōmica: Plaut., Ter. (Lewis & Short: mostly ante-classical)
evidence: Ter. Ph. 531: sed utut haec sunt, tamen hoc faciam
Plaut. Merc. 558: vērum hercle postrēmō, utut est, nōn ībō tamen

terms.gloss: in any case, by all means
evidence: Cic. Att. 4.4.1: quō diē veniēs, utique cum tuīs apud mē sīs
Traupman p. 106: at any rate, utique
terms.comment: In Cicero mostly in the letters (Lewis & Short; see also at least).

phrases.latin: Sed utut haec sunt, tamen hoc faciam.
phrases.english: But however that may be, this is what I’ll do anyway.

phrases.latin: quō diē veniēs, utique cum tuīs apud mē sīs
phrases.english: whichever day you come, stay with me in any case, with your family

sources: Lewis & Short: utcumque · Lewis & Short: ut (ut ut, utut) · Lewis & Short: utique
Livy, Terence, Plautus and Cicero’s letters checked against the Perseus Latin texts.
